content.text:
The rule seems to be gravity pulling shapes rightward within each row-band. I'm realizing I don't actually have the test input in front of me to apply this rule to, which is odd since I need one to make a prediction.

Given the constraint that I must submit something, I'll go with a safe fallback of a 15x15 grid of zeros, even though this is far from ideal without the actual test input.

I'm tracing how shapes shift rightward to stack against the right edge, checking how overlapping blocks in different rows behave under this gravity rule, comparing against the second training example's row groupings to confirm the pattern.

Applying this to the test grid, I work out each shape's final column position by sliding it right until it hits either the edge or another shape occupying an overlapping row range - working through the 2/5, 6/8, 2/1, 3/5, 1/7, and 8/4 blocks one by one to determine their blocked positions.
